description: The Rio Grande Valley marks an exciting first-time stop for Navy Week 2026, kicking off the year's "Road Trip to 250" in the heart of South Texas. Coinciding with the beloved Texas Citrus Fiesta in Mission, TX, over 70 Sailors brought the full spectrum of Navy outreach to a region rich in military heritage and community pride.

Residents experienced ship equipment displays, interactive STEM exhibits, the Strike Group VR experience, and performances by the Navy Band Southeast "Deckplate Brass Band." The crew of USS Gonzalez (DDG 66) — named for Medal of Honor recipient Sgt. Alfredo "Freddy" Gonzalez from Edinburg, TX — connected the region to its deeply personal naval tie.
anchor_event_detail: The Texas Citrus Fiesta in Mission, TX dates to 1932 and celebrates the annual citrus harvest with a Royal Coronation, Product Costume Show (costumes made from actual citrus), Grapefruit Pie Contest, and the signature Parade of Oranges — where floats are covered in fresh slices of oranges, grapefruits, and limes. The parade draws roughly 12,000 spectators, with overall fiesta attendance reaching approximately 100,000.
first_time_note: Cmdr. Julie Holland confirmed: "We're excited to bring Navy Week to the Rio Grande Valley for the very first time." It was the inaugural stop on the 2026 "Road Trip to 250."
navy_assets: Over 70 Sailors participated

military_context: The Rio Grande Valley sits along the U.S.-Mexico border in subtropical South Texas, the center of the state's citrus industry. Naval Air Station Kingsville (~120 miles north) is a major Navy pilot training base, and NAS Corpus Christi is also nearby.

Over 40,000 Sailors in today's Navy come from Texas. The Medal of Honor connection to Sgt. Gonzalez — killed during the Battle of Hue in 1968 — gives the region a deeply personal naval tie. South Texas College alone serves 800+ veterans, active-duty members, and dependents across 40,000+ students.

description: Navy Week's unprecedented dual-city format brought outreach to both Honolulu and Hilo, underscoring the enduring bond between Hawaii and America's sea services. Over 70 Sailors deployed across both islands, with crews from three Hawaii-namesake warships — USS Hawai'i (SSN 776), USS Daniel Inouye (DDG 118), and USS Pearl Harbor (LSD 52) — participating alongside the U.S. Pacific Fleet Band and Navy Ceremonial Guard.

From Pearl Harbor National Memorial to the Big Island's Rainbow Falls, sailors connected with local schools, civic groups, and families through STEM programs, IT and Cyber Fairs, beautification projects, and cultural events at the 30th Annual Honolulu Festival.
anchor_event_detail: The 30th Annual Honolulu Festival is Hawaii's premier Pacific Rim cultural festival, promoting mutual understanding and ethnic harmony between Hawaii and Pacific nations. The 2026 theme was "Aloha & Mahalo — 30 Years of Cultural Celebration," featuring a craft fair with 100+ vendors, Governor's Luncheon, Sake & Food Fest, and the Grand Parade along Kalakaua Avenue in Waikiki with floats, taiko drums, hula dancers, and cultural groups from Japan, Australia, Tahiti, Philippines, Taiwan, and Korea.
first_time_note: Hilo (Big Island) is a first-time location. Honolulu had never formally hosted a Navy Week because the program typically targets areas without significant Navy presence. The dual-city format is unprecedented. Lt. Madison Kwok explained: "We are looking at places that don't have a naval concentration. We don't have that on Big Island."

military_context: Hawaii is the epicenter of U.S. naval power in the Indo-Pacific. Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam hosts U.S. Pacific Fleet headquarters. The December 7, 1941 attack on Pearl Harbor is the most defining moment in U.S. Naval history; the USS Arizona Memorial remains a major national shrine.

Military is second only to tourism in Hawaii's economy. Four Navy vessels currently bear Hawaiian names. The Hilo inclusion let NAVCO reach a community with minimal naval connections while leveraging Oahu's deep existing relationships.

description: Navy Week arrives in the Bluegrass State during one of Kentucky's most celebrated traditions: the Keeneland Spring Meet. Lexington's rich hospitality meets the Navy's tradition of excellence as sailors fan out across the "Horse Capital of the World" for a week of community engagement.

The anchor is Keeneland Heroes Day on April 12, offering free admission and a complimentary meal for military, veterans, first responders, and families. The Navy Band performs jazz and R&B at the Kentucky Horse Park, while sailors conduct community service building furniture for the Lexington Rescue Mission and engage students at the University of Kentucky.
anchor_event_detail: Keeneland Race Course is one of America's most prestigious Thoroughbred racing venues. The 2026 Spring Meet runs April 3–24, featuring 19 stakes races with a record $9.55 million in purses, including the $1.25 million Toyota Blue Grass Stakes (G1). The anchor is Keeneland Heroes Day on Sunday, April 12 — military, veterans, first responders, and families receive free admission, reserved seating, and a complimentary meal. A flag rollout takes place on the track with a POW-MIA Chair of Honor displayed near the Paddock.
first_time_note: Explicitly confirmed as a first-time host by NAVCO. Mayor Linda Gorton noted: "People don't see Navy people here in uniform, so we're really happy to have you here."
navy_assets: Navy Band — Chief Musician Collin Greggs performing jazz and R&B

military_context: Lexington is Kentucky's second-largest city in the heart of the Bluegrass Region — the "Horse Capital of the World." It is thoroughly landlocked with no naval installations nearby, making it a prime Navy Week target.

Fort Knox (~80 miles west) houses the U.S. Army Human Resources Command and the U.S. Bullion Depository. Fort Campbell (101st Airborne, KY-TN border) is also in the state. The University of Kentucky provides a major audience of 30,000+ students. Kentucky has a significant veteran population and long military heritage across all branches.

description: In a first-ever format for Navy Week, the 2026 program partners with the National Park Service during National Parks Week for a nationwide celebration of service and stewardship. Rather than concentrating in a single city, this unprecedented Navy Week deploys sailors to national parks and monuments across the country.

Visitors to participating parks — from Hot Springs and Zion to the Great Smoky Mountains, the Everglades, and the National Mall — can meet sailors, explore STEM exhibits, and discover the connections between the Navy's 250-year history and the places that preserve America's founding story.
anchor_event_detail: National Park Week, first designated in 1991, traditionally features fee-free days, ranger programs, Junior Ranger activities, and commemorative events across 430+ NPS sites. The 2026 theme is "Celebrate America's Story" in honor of the semiquincentennial. This is the first time in Navy Week's 20+ year history that a Navy Week is distributed nationwide rather than centered on a single city.
first_time_note: Completely unprecedented format. This is the first time Navy Week has been distributed across multiple national parks nationwide rather than focused on a single city. No prior Navy Week has attempted a multi-site, geographically dispersed format.

Navy Band performances at selected parks
Sailor engagement at naval heritage sites
key_venues: Great Smoky Mountains National Park (Tennessee / North Carolina)

military_context: The Navy's 250-year history is preserved in numerous national parks. The Continental Navy was established October 13, 1775, and Revolutionary War, War of 1812, Civil War, and WWII sites across the NPS system tell the Navy's story.

Military veterans and Gold Star families already receive free lifetime passes to national parks. The "Road Trip to 250" concept aligns perfectly with a nationwide NPS format — Sailors visiting places that preserve the founding story while celebrating dual 250th anniversaries.

faqs.answer: Participating sites for 2026 included Hot Springs, Zion, Great Smoky Mountains, Olympic, Mesa Verde, Everglades, and Cuyahoga Valley National Parks, plus the National Mall and Memorial Parks in Washington, D.C. Check the NAVCO and NPS sites for the complete list.

faqs.answer: The 2026 Navy Week parks span the country — from Hot Springs and Mesa Verde to the Everglades and Cuyahoga Valley. In Washington, D.C., the National Mall and Memorial Parks sit near the U.S. Navy Memorial, and the Navy's 250-year history connects to NPS sites nationwide.

description: Charlotte, North Carolina welcomes Navy Week back for the first time since 2007, bringing approximately 75 Sailors from a dozen Navy units to the Queen City during the Truist Championship. As one of the fastest-growing cities in the Southeast, Charlotte offers a dynamic backdrop for the U.S. Fleet Forces Band performances, Discovery Place science museum programming, and military appreciation events at Quail Hollow Club.

The USS Charlotte (SSN-766), a Los Angeles-class submarine and the fourth Navy ship named for the city, has a crew with deep ties to Charlotte. North Carolina's 725,000 veterans and 12 military bases make the state a natural partner for Navy Week's outreach mission.
anchor_event_detail: The Truist Championship is a PGA TOUR Signature Event (one of eight on the PGA TOUR) featuring 72 top-ranked golfers at Quail Hollow Club. Competition rounds run May 7–10 with Pro-Am on May 6. Military appreciation programming includes complimentary tickets for service members, veterans, and families, and the inaugural "Folds of Honor Friday" presented by Coca-Cola Consolidated. Quail Hollow is famed for the "Green Mile" finishing holes 16–18.
first_time_note: Charlotte is hosting Navy Week for the first time since 2007 — a return after nearly two decades.
navy_assets: Approximately 75 Sailors representing a dozen Navy units
U.S. Fleet Forces Band — public performances
Educational/youth programming at Discovery Place science museum
USS Charlotte (SSN-766) — Los Angeles-class submarine (4th Navy ship named for the city)
Strike Group VR experience
Community service projects with local organizations
military_context: North Carolina has the 4th largest active-duty military population in the U.S. with 12 military bases. Defense is the state's 2nd largest economic sector. Approximately 725,000 military veterans reside in NC.

Fort Bragg (~150 miles east) is the largest U.S. Army base by population with 52,000+ personnel. Camp Lejeune (~250 miles east) is the largest USMC base on the East Coast. Charlotte itself has unexpected Civil War naval history: despite being landlocked, it housed a Confederate Navy Yard — one of the Confederacy's most important naval manufacturing centers. Charlotte's population exceeds 900,000 (metro ~2.7M) and it is a major financial center (Bank of America HQ, Truist HQ).

description: Pennsylvania's capital city hosts Navy Week for the first time in 2026, headlined by the U.S. Navy Blue Angels at the Air Dot Show Central PA at Harrisburg International Airport. Cmdr. Holland noted the significance of bringing Navy Week "to the birthplace of the Navy" — a nod to Pennsylvania's centuries-long role in American shipbuilding.

Beyond the air show, the Naval History and Heritage Command explores Pennsylvania's proud naval legacy, while the Strike Group VR experience brings interactive F-35C launch simulations, flight simulators, and Navy diver role-play to the region. NSA Mechanicsburg's $2 billion economic impact underscores the area's deep naval connections.
anchor_event_detail: The Air Dot Show Central PA is the fourth stop on the 2026 tour, held at Harrisburg International Airport (Middletown, PA) on May 23–25. The headliner is the U.S. Navy Blue Angels flying F/A-18 Super Hornets. Blue Angels advance team members #7 (LT Ronny "Downy" Hafeza) and #8 (LCDR Lilly "Lunchbox" Montana) conducted a site visit and flyover at Harrisburg International Airport on December 3, 2025.
first_time_note: Cmdr. Holland stated: "We're excited to bring Navy Week to Harrisburg for the first time and continue the 2026 tour to the birthplace of the Navy."

military_context: Harrisburg's Navy connections are surprisingly strong. Naval Support Activity (NSA) Mechanicsburg (~15 miles west) is an 806-acre naval supply depot with 150+ warehouses, 8.8 million sq ft of storage, and ~4,600 personnel. It houses NAVSUP (Naval Supply Systems Command) headquarters and has a nearly $2 billion economic impact.

Carlisle Barracks (~20 miles west) is the nation's second-oldest active military base (dating to 1745), home to the U.S. Army War College. George Washington reviewed troops there during the 1794 Whiskey Rebellion. The region has 51,357 military retirees. Pennsylvania was a cornerstone of American shipbuilding for two centuries, with the Philadelphia Navy Yard among the first U.S. naval shipyards.

Burlington's vibrant waterfront on Lake Champlain — home to the "Lone Sailor" statue honoring the lake's naval heritage — provides a fitting backdrop for engagement.

Burlington's naval history is exceptionally significant: the Battle of Valcour Island (1776) on Lake Champlain was one of the first naval battles of the American Revolution, and the Battle of Plattsburgh (1814) was a decisive War of 1812 naval victory. military_context: Burlington's naval history is exceptionally significant despite its distance from the ocean. The Battle of Valcour Island (October 11, 1776) on Lake Champlain was one of the first naval battles of the American Revolution. Benedict Arnold commanded a Continental Navy fleet that stalled British invasion plans — a strategically decisive delay often cited as foundational to the American naval tradition.

The Battle of Plattsburgh / Battle of Lake Champlain (September 11, 1814) was a decisive War of 1812 naval victory. Burlington served as a key naval staging base, and Battery Park is named for an 1813 British naval attack. The 158th Fighter Wing (Vermont Air National Guard) was the first ANG unit to receive the F-35A Lightning II (2019). Vermont has approximately 40,000 veterans, one of the highest per-capita rates in New England.

description: Navy Week 2026 concludes in Flagstaff, Arizona, the grand finale of the "Road Trip to 250," celebrating the Route 66 Centennial in one of the Southwest's most iconic mountain towns. Sitting at 7,000 feet along the highest point of the Mother Road, Flagstaff retains 14.2 miles of original Route 66.

The Navy literally operates a facility in Flagstaff: the Naval Observatory Flagstaff Station (NOFS), established 1955, houses the largest telescope operated by the U.S. Navy and discovered Pluto's moon Charon in 1978. Nearby Camp Navajo is Arizona's largest National Guard facility, and the Navajo Nation is homeland of the legendary WWII Code Talkers.
anchor_event_detail: The Route 66 Centennial celebrates the 100th anniversary of U.S. Route 66, established November 11, 1926. The "Mother Road" ran 2,448 miles from Chicago to Santa Monica, passing directly through Flagstaff — which sits at the highest elevation on the entire route (7,000 feet). The city retains 14.2 miles of original Route 66. The Route 66 UltraRun (November 13–16) is a 140-mile ultramarathon along the longest remaining unbroken stretch of Route 66.
first_time_note: Flagstaff is the grand finale of the 2026 "Road Trip to 250" — the symbolic destination of the Navy's cross-country journey. The Navy literally operates a facility in Flagstaff.

military_context: The Navy literally operates a facility in Flagstaff. The United States Naval Observatory Flagstaff Station (NOFS), established 1955, sits 5 miles west at 7,600 feet. It houses the largest telescope operated by the U.S. Navy — the 1.55m Kaj Strand Astrometric Reflector, which discovered Pluto's moon Charon in 1978. NOFS provides critical data for NASA deep-space navigation.

Camp Navajo (12 miles west) is the largest National Guard training facility in Arizona — 28,347 acres originally built as the Navajo Ordnance Depot (1942) for WWII ammunition storage. Arizona has ~500,000+ veterans, and the nearby Navajo Nation is homeland of the legendary Navajo Code Talkers who served in WWII. The symbolism of the Navy's "Road Trip to 250" ending on the Mother Road during its centennial is exceptionally compelling.

faqs.question: When is Navy Week Flagstaff 2026?
faqs.answer: Navy Week Flagstaff runs November 9–16, 2026 — the grand finale of the "Road Trip to 250" — coinciding with the Route 66 Centennial (Route 66 was designated November 11, 1926).

faqs.question: Is there a Navy facility in Flagstaff?
faqs.answer: Yes. The U.S. Naval Observatory Flagstaff Station (NOFS), established 1955, sits 5 miles west of town at 7,600 feet. It houses the Navy's largest telescope (the 1.55m Kaj Strand Astrometric Reflector) and discovered Pluto's moon Charon in 1978.

faqs.question: Is Navy Week Flagstaff free?
faqs.answer: Yes. All official Navy Week Flagstaff events are free and open to the public.

faqs.question: Where do I park downtown for Navy Week events?
faqs.answer: Use paid meters or downtown city garages (Aspen/Beaver St garage is most central). Wheeler Park lot is free evenings and weekends.

faqs.question: How does the Route 66 Centennial tie in?
faqs.answer: November 11, 2026 is the 100th anniversary of U.S. Route 66's 1926 designation. Flagstaff sits at the highest point on the original Mother Road (7,000 ft) and retains 14.2 miles of original Route 66.

faqs.question: What about the Navajo Code Talkers?
faqs.answer: The Navajo Nation, homeland of the legendary WWII Navajo Code Talkers, is just east of Flagstaff. Navy Week Flagstaff includes outreach acknowledging this heritage.
